name: OpenAQ
description: Air quality measurements aggregated from government reference monitors and low-cost sensor networks worldwide, normalised onto one schema so a PM2.5 reading from Delhi and one from Denver are directly comparable. Tens of thousands of locations across roughly 100 countries, with hourly measurements going back to 2016 and a growing archive of parquet snapshots on S3 for anyone who wants history in bulk rather than by the page.

temporal.updated: continuously; ingestion lag varies by provider from minutes to a day

license.name: CC-BY-4.0 for the aggregation; each provider's own terms apply to their readings
license.redistribution: permitted with attribution to OpenAQ and to the originating agency, which the record's `provider` field names

access.auth_note: v3 requires a free key sent as the X-API-Key header. Register at https://explore.openaq.org/register. There is no keyless route -- v2 was the keyless one and it is gone.
access.size_hint: a page of measurements is a few hundred KB; the open S3 archive at s3://openaq-data-archive is hundreds of GB
access.rate_limit: 60 requests per minute and 2,000 per hour per key (documented); exceeding it returns 429 with a Retry-After
access.pagination: page and limit, limit max 1000; `found` in the meta block may come back as a string like '>1000' rather than a number

probes.description: v3 without a key -- proves the gate, and that the service is up
probes.note: A clean, readable 401 naming the header it wants. If this ever answers 200, the keyless route came back.

probes.description: The keyless v2 endpoint every tutorial still shows
probes.known_broken: 410 Gone on 2026-09-10: 'Version 1 and Version 2 API endpoints are retired and no longer available. Please migrate to Version 3 endpoints.' Recorded because a large amount of published code, and most search results, still call v2.

recipes.title: Hourly PM2.5 history for one sensor
recipes.code:
# find the sensor id from /v3/locations/{id} first -- measurements hang off sensors, not locations
curl -s -H "X-API-Key: $OPENAQ_API_KEY" 'https://api.openaq.org/v3/sensors/3920/measurements?datetime_from=2024-01-01&datetime_to=2024-01-08&limit=1000' | head -c 600

recipes.title: Skip the API for history
recipes.code:
# the S3 archive is public and needs no key or AWS account
aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://openaq-data-archive/records/csv.gz/locationid=2178/year=2024/

gotchas.trap: Nearly every example you will find online calls api.openaq.org/v2/... keylessly. That endpoint now answers 410 Gone, so code copied from a blog post, a notebook or an LLM fails on the first call for reasons that look like a network problem.
gotchas.fix: v3 only, with X-API-Key. Confirmed 2026-09-10: v2 returns 410 with an explicit migration message; v3 without the header returns 401.

gotchas.trap: In v3 measurements no longer hang off a location. They hang off a sensor, and one location has several sensors -- one per pollutant.
gotchas.fix: GET /v3/locations/{id} to list its sensors, then /v3/sensors/{sensor_id}/measurements. The v2 habit of querying measurements by location or by city has no v3 equivalent.

gotchas.trap: Reference-grade government monitors and low-cost sensors sit side by side in the same result set, and their readings are not equivalent -- low-cost PM sensors drift badly with humidity.
gotchas.fix: Filter on the provider and on `isMonitor` before comparing anything across locations. A city-level average that mixes both is measuring the sensor mix as much as the air.

gotchas.trap: Units are not uniform. The same pollutant arrives as ug/m3 from some providers and ppm or ppb from others, and OpenAQ passes both through.
gotchas.fix: Read the `parameter.units` on every measurement rather than assuming. Converting between ppb and ug/m3 needs the molecular weight and the temperature, so it is not a constant.

gotchas.trap: The meta block's `found` is sometimes a string such as '>1000' rather than an integer, which breaks arithmetic on the total.
gotchas.fix: Coerce defensively, or page until you get a short result set.

gotchas.trap: Coverage gaps read as clean air. A country with no sensors and a country with excellent air both show nothing.
gotchas.fix: Check location counts per country before drawing any global comparison. Absence of data is the most common finding here and the easiest to misread.

fields: locations[].sensors[].id -- the key you actually need; measurements are per sensor
parameter.name and parameter.units -- pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, so2; units vary by provider
provider -- who operates the monitor; the basis for judging quality
isMonitor -- true for reference-grade, false for low-cost sensor
datetimeFirst / datetimeLast -- the location's coverage window, worth checking before a query
coordinates.latitude / .longitude -- and note the API takes coordinates as lat,lon
